Gitoids calculated on software artifacts (Snippet, File, or Package Elements) should be recorded in the SPDX 3 SoftwareArtifact's contentIdentifier property. Gitoids calculated on the Artifact Input Manifest (Input Manifest Identifier) should be recorded in the SPDX 3 Element's externalIdentifier property. See [OmniBOR Specification](https://github.com/omnibor/spec/), a minimalistic specification for describing software [Artifact Dependency Graphs](https://github.com/omnibor/spec/blob/eb1ee5c961c16215eb8709b2975d193a2007a35d/spec/SPEC.md#artifact-dependency-graph-adg).

A gitoid may represent either an [Artifact Identifier](https://github.com/omnibor/spec/blob/eb1ee5c961c16215eb8709b2975d193a2007a35d/spec/SPEC.md#artifact-identifier-types) for the software artifact or an [Input Manifest Identifier](https://github.com/omnibor/spec/blob/eb1ee5c961c16215eb8709b2975d193a2007a35d/spec/SPEC.md#input-manifest-identifier) for the software artifact's associated [Artifact Input Manifest](https://github.com/omnibor/spec/blob/eb1ee5c961c16215eb8709b2975d193a2007a35d/spec/SPEC.md#artifact-input-manifest); this ambiguity exists because the Artifact Input Manifest is itself an artifact, and the gitoid of that artifact is its valid identifier. Gitoids calculated on software artifacts (Snippet, File, or Package Elements) should be recorded in the SPDX 3 SoftwareArtifact's contentIdentifier property. Gitoids calculated on the Artifact Input Manifest (Input Manifest Identifier) should be recorded in the SPDX 3 Element's externalIdentifier property. See [OmniBOR Specification](https://github.com/omnibor/spec/), a minimalistic specification for describing software [Artifact Dependency Graphs](https://github.com/omnibor/spec/blob/eb1ee5c961c16215eb8709b2975d193a2007a35d/spec/SPEC.md#artifact-dependency-graph-adg).

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: follows
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The `to` Element succeeds the `from` Element, establishing a unidirectional sequence. This succession is defined as chronological, procedural, or logical. It is used to represent either a temporal order (e.g., in a workflow) or a logical order for processing and traversal (e.g., in an ordered list).
The relative file name of a file to be excluded from the `PackageVerificationCode`.
Uniquely identifies an external element.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: duns
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: [Data Universal Numbering System (D-U-N-S) Number](https://www.dnb.com/en-us/smb/duns.html) is a unique nine-digit identifier, issued by Dun & Bradstreet, that identifies a business entity, often on a location-specific basis.

Property describing the start time of a build.
Information about the relationship between two Elements.
Indicates whether a relationship is known to be complete, incomplete, or if no assertion is made with respect to relationship completeness.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: ai
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The element follows the AI profile specification.
Provides the license under which the SPDX documentation of the Element can be used.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: hardware
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The element follows the Hardware profile specification.
Specifies the SSVC decision type.
EvidenceType refers to categories of documented or observable proof used to verify compliance, qualification, or performance

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: compliance
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A contact point for compliance (i.e. export control, licensing).
Energy consumed during inference time by an AI model that is being used in the AI system.
Commentary on an assertion that an annotator has made.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: support
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: A reference to the software support channel or other support information for a package.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: affects
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The `from` Vulnerability, Action or DefinedProcess affects each `to` Element.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: pretrainedOn
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The `from` Element has been pretrained on the `to` Element(s).
It is the authoritative or credible entity, document, or body of knowledge that provides the meaning of a type, ensuring accuracy, context, and standardization.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: ownership
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: Ownership refers to the legal right to control, manage, and benefit from an asset, resource, or responsibility. It establishes authority, accountability, and entitlements over something, whether it's property, a business, intellectual property, or responsibilities.
Property that describes the digest of the build configuration file used to invoke a build.
Specifies the type of an external reference.
Confidentiality level of the data points contained in the dataset.
Type of data in a dataset.

Type of the model used in the AI software.
Unit in which energy is measured.
Link to the project contract.

Artifact representing a serialization instance of SPDX data containing the definition of a particular Element.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: ocsp
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: Online Certificate Status Protocol, or OCSP, is a common scheme used to maintain the security of a server and other network resources.
Unit of energy consumption.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: requirementUUID
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The UUID used by a requirements management or any other lifecycle management tool to uniquely identify a requirement item. UUID, or universally unique ID, is a standard term in requirements engineering.
Provides an indication of where to retrieve an external Element.
Energy consumed when training the AI model that is being used in the AI system.
Provides information about the type of an SBOM.
The product lifecycle phase, the requirement is applicable for.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: adler32
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: Adler-32 checksum is part of the widely used zlib compression library as defined in [RFC 1950](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/rfc1950/) Section 2.3.
The amount or measure of a bulk product.
Defines the beginning of a range.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: container
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The Element is a container image which can be used by a container runtime application.
Information related to virtual hardware simulation.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: availableFrom
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The `from` Element is available from the additional supplier described by each `to` Element.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: blake2b512
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: BLAKE2b algorithm with a digest size of 512, as defined in [RFC 7693](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/rfc7693/) Section 4.
Designates elements as products where the impact of a vulnerability is being investigated.
Links a vulnerability and elements representing products (in the VEX sense) where a fix has been applied and are no longer affected.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: design
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: SBOM of intended, planned software project or product with included components (some of which may not yet exist) for a new software artifact.
EvaluationResultType describes the outcome of an evaluation or verification process with.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: hasResolution
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The `from` ResolutionAction point to the `to` OutOfSpecAction that is addressed.

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: invokedBy
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: The `from` Element was invoked by the `to` Agent, during a LifecycleScopeType period (for example, a Build element that describes a build step).

rdf:Description.rdfs:label: build
rdf:Description.rdfs:comment: SBOM generated as part of the process of building the software to create a releasable artifact (e.g., executable or package) from data such as source files, dependencies, built components, build process ephemeral data, and other SBOMs.
